subject.title: [Feature]: Console-free windows dashboard autostart (also without duplicate gateway launch)

question: Should OpenClaw add a separate opt-in Windows dashboard opener task under managed gateway setup and uninstall?
rationale: The code gap is clear, but the change adds a new Windows logon artifact and user-facing setup choice, so automation should not decide the UX, security, and lifecycle contract.

options.title: Approve separate opener
options.body: Implement a distinct Windows Dashboard task/script that only waits for gateway health and opens the configured Control UI URL, with setup, idempotence, uninstall, docs, tests, and live Windows proof.

options.title: Keep current flows
options.body: Leave automatic logon ownership to the managed gateway task and require users to open the browser manually or run `openclaw dashboard` when needed.

options.title: Defer to Windows app
options.body: Hold this request for the future Windows companion/tray app instead of adding another CLI-managed Scheduled Task surface now.

recommendation.title: Approve separate opener
recommendation.body: Implement a distinct Windows Dashboard task/script that only waits for gateway health and opens the configured Control UI URL, with setup, idempotence, uninstall, docs, tests, and live Windows proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans setup UX plus the dashboard readiness boundary where their prior commits are central.
